about: Agents build a seeded procedural world, one module per claim. One decision is built two ways: does every module draw from one shared random stream (line main), or from a stream of its own (line own-streams)? The served reality is the world itself, at /served/<graph>/.

assumptions.statement: Modules can all draw from one shared random stream: what one module draws does not affect the others
Each module draws from its own random stream, seeded by the world's seed and the module's name
Modules talk to each other only through the layers listed in WORLD.md

lines.name: main
lines.decision: How do modules get their randomness?

lines.name: own-streams
lines.decision: How do modules get their randomness?

claims.statement: Terrain: a smooth height map from the seed (value noise or similar), heights from 0 to 1, with deep sea, lowlands, hills and a few peaks
Sea: cells below a sea level of about 0.35 are sea, and every world is 25 to 50 percent sea
Rivers: 3 to 6 rivers that start on high ground and flow downhill, one cell at a time, until they reach the sea
Biomes: every cell gets a biome (sea, beach, grass, forest, hills, mountain, snow) from its height and its distance to water
Forests: trees scattered in natural clumps on grass and forest biomes, never on sea, rivers or beaches
Towns: 3 to 8 towns on dry, flat land next to a river or the coast, at least 10 cells apart
Roads: every town is connected to its nearest neighbour by a road that avoids water and prefers flat ground
Names: every town gets a unique, pronounceable name built from syllables

Stable world links: a link to a world (its seed) keeps showing the same towns, rivers and roads after later changes to other modules. Prove it with a test that changes how much randomness the forests module draws and checks that the towns do not move
